city.name: Asakusa
city.description: Asakusa and the Skytree from open data, lit by the real sun: Senso-ji, the Kaminarimon's lantern, Nakamise, the Sumida and its water bus, and Tokyo Skytree across the river.

tour.title: Asakusa, from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings. {share:plateau}% of the footprint area stands at a height Project PLATEAU surveyed, on GSI's 5 m laser-scanned bare earth.

tour.title: Senso-ji
tour.text: The approach runs north from the Kaminarimon, between Nakamise's shops, through the Hozomon to the main hall, with the five-storey pagoda to its left. The gates, pagoda and hall are built to their published sizes: the pagoda {landmark:sensoji.pagoda.top_m} m to the tip of its finial.

tour.title: Tokyo Skytree
tour.text: 634 m: a triangle 68 m a side at the foot, a circle by 320 m. The Tembo Deck is at 350 m, the Galleria at 450 m. After dark it is lit, one night in Iki's blue, the next in Miyabi's purple.

tour.title: The Sumida and the Asahi flame
tour.text: Across Azumabashi: the Asahi Beer Hall, black granite under Philippe Starck's golden flame (1989), and the headquarters beside it, amber glass with a white crown, a glass of beer. The water bus leaves from the pier at the bridge's foot.

seawall.note: The rivers' and the bay's revetments and the castle moats: granite blocks and concrete.

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from the cities' street-tree surveys and the parks' own guides: ginkgo and zelkova (keyaki) are Japan's commonest street trees, with plane trees and camphor; the woods are the laurel forest's evergreen broadleaves and camphors, with zelkovas, black pines, maples and a few cedars (sugi, standing for hinoki too). Areas give the parks and precincts known for their own trees a mix of their own; their outlines are OpenStreetMap's (pipeline/tree_areas.py). Somei-yoshino cherries (sakura) line Tokyo's streets after the ginkgo and the zelkova, and stand in the parks' lawns and along the rivers and moats; areas give the places known for them a mix of their own.

areas.name: Sumida Park
areas.note: Some 600 cherries along the Sumida's west bank, planted by the shogun Yoshimune (Taito City).
